tools.name: query

tools.description: PERMANENTLY delete a site and ALL its analytics data (every event and annotation). Irreversible. Confirm with the owner before calling; pass confirm: the site's exact domain.

tools.name: portfolio_overview

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "query" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "delete_site" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: PERMANENTLY delete a site and ALL its analytics data (every event and annotation). Irreversible. Confirm with the owner before calling; pass confirm: the site's…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: what_broke · Private data: update_site_context, record_annotation · Public sink: what_changed · Destructive: funnel, journeys, delete_site.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: what_broke · Private data: update_site_context, record_annotation · Public sink: what_changed · Destructive: funnel, journeys, delete_site

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
